p113: 113.  The third-party intervener acknowledged that the granting of an amnesty could, in some cases, lead to impunity for those responsible for violations of fundamental human rights and thus undermine attempts to safeguard such rights. However, there were strong policy reasons in favour of the use of amnesty where it constituted the only way out of violent dictatorships and interminable conflicts. The third-party intervener stated that it was opposed to a total prohibition of amnesties and in favour of a more nuanced approach to the question of granting amnesties.
p114: 114.  In the case of Sergeï Zolotoukhine v. Russia the Court held that Article 4 of Protocol No. 7 must be understood as prohibiting the prosecution or trial of a second “offence” in so far as it arises from identical facts or facts which are substantially the same ([GC], no. 14939/03, § 82, ECHR 2009).

p116: 116.  Therefore, in so far as both sets of proceedings concern the above-mentioned charges, the applicant was indeed prosecuted twice for the same offences.
p117: 117.  There are two distinct situations as regards the charges brought against the applicant in both the first and the second set of proceedings.
p118: 118.  Firstly, on 25 January 1996 the prosecutor withdrew the charges concerning the alleged murders of N.V. and Ne.V. on 10 December 1991 (see paragraphs 120-121 below).
p119: 119.  Secondly, by a decision of 24 June 1997 under the General Amnesty Act, the Osijek County Court terminated the proceedings concerning the alleged murders of S.B. and V.B. and the grievous bodily harm inflicted on Sl.B. on 20 November 1991 (see paragraphs 122 et seq. below).
p120: 120.  The Court has already held that the discontinuation of criminal proceedings by a public prosecutor amounts to neither a conviction nor an acquittal, and that Article 4 of Protocol No. 7 therefore finds no application in that situation (see Smirnova and Smirnova v. Russia (dec.), nos. 46133/99 and 48183/99, 3 October 2002, and Harutyunyan v. Armenia (dec.), no. 34334/04, 7 December 2006).
p121: 121.  Consequently, the prosecution’s dropping of the charges concerning the murders of N.V. and Ne.V. does not fall within the scope of Article 4 of Protocol No. 7 to the Convention. It follows that this part of the complaint is incompatible ratione materiae with the provisions of the Convention.
p122: 122.  As to the remaining charges (the murders of V.B. and S.B. and the grievous bodily harm inflicted on Sl.B.), the first set of criminal proceedings against the applicant was terminated under the General Amnesty Act.
